![Health Benefits of Creatine](https://api.dataforseo.com/cdn/i/10241846-8540-0139-0000-25719bd0573c:4)
Creatine is `generally safe and well-tolerated for healthy adults when taken at recommended doses of 3 to 5 grams per day`.[[1]](https://www.health.harvard.edu/exercise-and-fitness/what-is-creatine-potential-benefits-and-risks-of-this-popular-supplement)[[2]](https://www.urmc.rochester.edu/news/publications/health-matters/creatine-for-beginners-should-you-take-it)

### Key Safety Facts

- **Kidney and Liver Health:** Extensive research shows no adverse effects on kidney or liver function in healthy individuals at standard doses. However, people with pre-existing kidney disease should avoid or consult a doctor before use.[[1]](https://www.cedars-sinai.org/stories-and-insights/healthy-living/should-you-take-creatine-what-to-know-before-you-supplement)[[2]](https://store.mayoclinic.com/education/creatine-beyond-the-gym-what-older-adults-and-non-athletes-should-know/)
- **Common Side Effects:** The most frequent side effects are temporary water retention in muscles and mild weight gain. High doses can occasionally cause gastrointestinal discomfort like stomachaches or diarrhea.[[1]](https://mydoctor.kaiserpermanente.org/mas/news/what-is-creatine-uses-benefits-and-side-effects-explained-2926814)[[2]](https://store.mayoclinic.com/education/creatine-beyond-the-gym-what-older-adults-and-non-athletes-should-know/)
- **Special Populations:** Medical organizations generally advise against creatine use for individuals under 18, pregnant or breastfeeding women, or those taking specific medications affecting kidney function, due to a lack of long-term data in these groups.[[1]](https://www.cedars-sinai.org/stories-and-insights/healthy-living/should-you-take-creatine-what-to-know-before-you-supplement)
- **Regulation:** Dietary supplements are not strictly approved or regulated for safety and effectiveness by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). Choosing [third-party tested products](https://www.mdanderson.org/cancerwise/creatine-powders-and-supplements--should-you-take-one.h00-159853767.html) helps ensure purity.[[1]](https://www.mdanderson.org/cancerwise/creatine-powders-and-supplements--should-you-take-one.h00-159853767.html)[[2]](https://www.health.harvard.edu/exercise-and-fitness/what-is-creatine-potential-benefits-and-risks-of-this-popular-supplement)[[3]](https://mydoctor.kaiserpermanente.org/mas/news/what-is-creatine-uses-benefits-and-side-effects-explained-2926814)[[4]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_i_sNy5mjvQ&t=52)

For more context on how this supplement works in the body, see the guide on [Harvard Health](https://www.health.harvard.edu/exercise-and-fitness/what-is-creatine-potential-benefits-and-risks-of-this-popular-supplement).[[1]](https://www.health.harvard.edu/exercise-and-fitness/what-is-creatine-potential-benefits-and-risks-of-this-popular-supplement)Are you considering taking creatine for **athletic performance**, **muscle building** , or **general health** ?
